title: A Recipe for the Homecoming
premise: Ines Okonkwo just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built on the ruins of the town's original bakery. But when a group chat called 'The Proofing Room' starts sending her messages describing events days before they happen — a fire drill, a broken window, her own name read over the intercom — she discovers five students have inherited fragments of the bakery's memory through an old recipe book passed down since the founding families. The chat is the book trying to reassemble itself, and it needs Ines because her grandmother was its last keeper. As the predictions turn darker and the school board moves to demolish the ruins before graduation, Ines must unite the fractured keepers, recover the lost final page of the recipe, and bake the Homecoming Loaf one last time — because the tradition that made the town will unmake it if it dies forgotten.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is a former line cook who spent six years in restaurant kitchens before trading service windows for writing desks. He lives near an old mill town where every third building claims to be haunted, and he writes stories about the places that remember us better than we remember them.

chapters.title: Head Down, Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Three weeks into Hollow Creek High, Ines has perfected invisibility: sit center-left, answer only when called, never linger. A tour guide's offhand comment about the school being built 'on the old Kessler bakery' snags something in her — her late grandmother's recipe box has a card labeled 'Hollow Creek.' Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by a first flicker of belonging-to-somewhere.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. An unknown number adds her to a chat called 'The Proofing Room' with four other students she barely knows. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill to the minute. It happens exactly. When Ines tries to leave the chat, the exit button simply isn't there. Emotional beat: unease curdling into the guilty thrill of finally being chosen for something.

chapters.title: Four Strangers and a Prediction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV among the chat members: Theo (stoner philosopher), Marisol (student council perfectionist), Dev (quiet coder), and Priya (track star). They compare notes in the library basement: each received a different fragment of an old recipe, each got added at random. Or so they think. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared impossibility.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with flashback. At home, Ines opens her grandmother's recipe box properly for the first time since the funeral and finds a hollow bottom holding a torn page edge and a photograph of five teenagers in front of the old bakery, 1974. Her grandmother's face is among them. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance; the dead leaving instructions.

chapters.title: The Rules of Rising
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The group deciphers the chat's pattern: predictions come in threes, always tied to the school building, always escalating. Dev maps prediction locations onto the floor plan and finds they trace the bakery's original rooms — the ovens sat under the gymnasium. Emotional beat: wonder giving way to the realization they're inside something with structure and intent.

chapters.title: Marisol Breaks a Rule
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Panicked by a prediction involving her own public humiliation, Marisol acts to prevent it — and the event happens anyway, worse, plus a new prediction arrives like a penalty. She confesses to the group: you can't dodge the proofing. Emotional beat: control shattering; the group learns the cost of interference.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The school board announces the ruins beneath the east wing will be excavated and paved over starting spring break — before graduation. That night the chat sends its first non-prediction message, addressed to Ines alone: 'The last keeper's granddaughter owes a loaf.' Emotional beat: stakes made concrete; a deadline now exists.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the East Wing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Nighttime infiltration through the maintenance tunnels. Behind a bricked wall they find the bakery's original hearth, cold but intact, and a ledger listing keeper names across generations — ending with 'R. Okonkwo.' Priya realizes Ines didn't join the chat randomly; the chat recruited her. Emotional beat: awe undercut by betrayal-adjacent suspicion toward Ines.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Chat
chapters.summary: Group POV via chat transcript framing. The others accuse Ines of knowing all along. Ines, furious and hurt, reveals the torn page from her grandmother's box — proof she's as much in the dark as they are. The chat goes silent for two full days, longest ever. Emotional beat: found family fracturing before it fully formed.

chapters.title: Silence Has a Taste
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. With the chat dormant, small wrongnesses accumulate: bread in the cafeteria molding overnight into shapes, the smell of yeast in locked rooms, Dev's code predicting things unprompted. Dev realizes the chat wasn't the source — it was a valve. Something older is speaking directly now. Emotional beat: dread replacing mystery.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines visits her grandmother's old friend, Mrs. Adeyemi, who explains the tradition: the founding families baked a communal loaf each year from a shared recipe, each family keeping one page. The loaf 'kept the town's memory warm' — literally; those who ate it remembered things they'd never lived. The chat is the recipe itself, alive, seeking completion. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as obligation and gift at once.

chapters.title: Five Pages, One Recipe
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Each teen examines their inherited fragment: flour ratios, water sources, oven temperatures — and stranger instructions ('knead while naming the absent'). They realize the final page, the one Ines holds torn, contains the blessing that makes it work. Without it, the demolition won't just erase a building; it will sever the town's memory entirely. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing into mission.

chapters.title: Predictions Turn Personal
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat resumes, but predictions now target the five: Priya's scholarship interview sabotaged, Dev's college acceptance revoked, Marisol's parents' shop cited. The recipe is pressuring them — or warning them what forgetting costs. Theo argues it's blackmail; Ines insists it's desperation. Emotional beat: rising tension; the group divided on whether to obey or fight.

chapters.title: The Archive Fire
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A predicted fire — small, contained — consumes the town archive's local history section the night before Marisol planned to photocopy the bakery records. Someone else is interfering with the recipe's survival. Suspicion falls on the school board chair, whose family left the tradition generations ago. Emotional beat: the antagonist made visible; stakes turn adversarial.

chapters.title: Chairman Voss
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confronts Chairman Voss, who coolly admits his grandfather walked away from the loaf after a bad year and has watched the town slowly forget itself since — the shuttered shops, the demolished landmarks. He believes erasure is mercy. 'Memory is a debt,' he tells her. 'I'm forgiving it.' Emotional beat: chilling empathy for the antagonist; ideology versus inheritance.

chapters.title: Kneading While Naming the Absent
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rehearsal run: the five attempt the recipe in Theo's garage with substitutions, following their fragments. It fails — dough grey, tasteless — until they knead while speaking names of the town's forgotten: the baker, the founders, Ines's grandmother. The dough rises impossibly fast. Emotional beat: grief transformed into practice; the theme of memory made physical.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following a final prediction — coordinates under the gym floor — Ines finds her grandmother's time capsule from 1974: the missing piece of the final page, hidden by five teenagers who knew the tradition would need saving someday. Her grandmother wrote her a letter: 'You'll be scared. Bake anyway.' Emotional beat: the emotional climax of inheritance; the dead speaking directly to the living.

chapters.title: Spring Break Eve
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Demolition crews arrive early. The five have one night. Voss, tipped off, gets the east wing sealed with police tape. Marisol uses her student council access to forge a permit delay; Priya creates a diversion at the board meeting; Dev kills the site's power grid. Each uses the exact skill the recipe's fragments mirrored. Emotional beat: found family functioning as one organism.

chapters.title: The Last Proofing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the cold hearth room, the five assemble the complete recipe and light the original oven. As the loaf bakes, the building remembers out loud — voices, smells, the 1974 five laughing somewhere in the walls. Voss breaks in to stop them and Ines offers him the first slice instead of a fight. Emotional beat: climax held on a knife-edge between destruction and offering.

chapters.title: What Voss Remembered
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The slice returns everything his grandfather buried: the reason he left (shame over a burned harvest loaf), the town singing in the bakery, his own childhood erased by his family's silence. Voss weeps, then calls off the morning demolition himself. Emotional beat: antagonist converted not by defeat but by remembrance — the story's thesis embodied.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Group POV. Graduation week: the five bake the Homecoming Loaf publicly in the restored hearth, now a protected landmark, and the whole town eats and remembers together. The chat sends one last message — 'Recipe complete. Keepers: five' — and dissolves forever. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss; the magic ends so the tradition can live humanly.

chapters.title: A Recipe for the Next One
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. Summer. Ines copies the recipe into a new box, adding her own page, and leaves a blank one labeled for whoever comes next. At the farmers market she watches a nervous new kid hover at the edge of the crowd — and slips a starter portion of bread into their bag. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; inheritance renewed as choice, not burden.
